question: What are current (2025-2026) average Facebook/Meta ads benchmarks: CPM, CTR, CPC, conversion rate, and cost per acquisition? Give numbers by industry where possible.

output.content:
## Current Meta/Facebook ads benchmarks (2025–2026)

Benchmarks vary substantially by **campaign objective, geography, placement, attribution window, and whether “conversion” means a lead or a purchase**. The most useful comparison is to separate **traffic**, **lead generation**, and **e-commerce purchase** campaigns.

### Overall benchmarks

| Objective / dataset | CPM | CTR | CPC | Conversion rate | CPA / CPL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Traffic campaigns** — US, 2025 | — | **1.71%** | **$0.70** | — | — |
| **Lead-generation campaigns** — US, 2025 | — | **2.59%** | **$1.92** | **7.72%** | **$27.66 CPL** |
| **E-commerce purchase campaigns** — 2025–26 | **$13–$15** | **~2.2–2.4%** | — | **~1.5–1.6%** | **~$38–$39 CPA** |

WordStream/LocaliQ’s 2025 US dataset reports 1.71% CTR and $0.70 CPC for traffic campaigns, and 2.59% CTR, $1.92 CPC, 7.72% CVR, and $27.66 CPL for lead campaigns. [[1, 2]] Triple Whale’s large e-commerce dataset reports a $15.06 CPM, 2.39% CTR, 1.53% CVR, and $38.99 CPA for August 2025–July 2026. [[3, 4]]

### Lead-generation benchmarks by industry

| Industry | CTR | CPC | Conversion rate | Cost per lead |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Arts & entertainment | 3.92% | $1.08 | 9.34% | $18.17 |
| Real estate | 3.75% | $1.57 | 9.53% | $16.61 |
| Sports & recreation | 3.41% | $1.07 | 5.48% | $19.30 |
| Restaurants & food | 2.97% | $0.74 | **18.25%** | **$3.16** |
| Career & employment | 2.81% | $0.86 | 5.77% | $17.64 |
| Beauty & personal care | 2.55% | $3.06 | 5.29% | $51.42 |
| Attorneys / legal | 2.11% | $4.10 | 10.53% | $18.17 |
| Education & instruction | 1.86% | $1.65 | 10.08% | $28.22 |
| Industrial & commercial | 2.08% | $1.80 | 9.34% | $37.34 |
| Home & home improvement | 1.94% | $2.23 | 5.22% | $41.26 |
| Health & fitness | 1.72% | $2.64 | 5.63% | $52.98 |
| Furniture | 1.48% | $2.18 | 3.77% | $40.04 |
| Dentists & dental | 1.05% | **$9.78** | 6.38% | **$76.71** |

These are 2025 US lead-campaign benchmarks; the all-industry averages are 2.59% CTR, $1.92 CPC, 7.72% conversion rate, and $27.66 CPL. [[1, 5]]

### E-commerce purchase benchmarks by industry

| Industry | CPM | CTR | Conversion rate | CPA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baby | $11.50 | 1.98% | 1.82% | $29.61 |
| Toys, art & collectibles | $12.54 | 2.35% | 1.53% | $34.85 |
| Apparel & accessories | $13.25 | 2.44% | 1.47% | $36.98 |
| Lifestyle & boutique | $13.25 | 2.44% | 1.62% | $31.16 |
| Business supplies & equipment | $13.33 | 1.88% | 1.70% | $37.98 |
| Books & music | $14.01 | 2.62% | 1.69% | $30.69 |
| E-learning & online courses | $14.05 | 2.74% | 1.31% | $26.80 |
| Home & garden | $14.67 | 2.38% | 1.24% | $47.93 |
| Electronics | $15.09 | 2.41% | 1.13% | $51.86 |
| Food & beverage | $15.32 | 1.98% | 1.89% | $38.57 |
| Pets & animals | $16.27 | 2.37% | 1.63% | $38.51 |
| Travel accessories & luggage | $16.34 | 2.40% | 1.19% | $50.95 |
| Beauty | $18.80 | 2.46% | 1.79% | $39.31 |
| Health & wellness | $21.80 | **3.02%** | 1.50% | $40.53 |

Triple Whale’s e-commerce benchmarks cover 17 verticals and 40,000+ brands; its overall median was $15.06 CPM, 2.39% CTR, 1.53% CVR, and $38.99 CPA. [[3, 4]]

### Practical 2025–26 ranges

- **CPM:** roughly **$8–$15** for broad mixed campaigns; **$13–$20+** is common for competitive e-commerce, finance, health, and Q4 campaigns. A global monthly median reached $25.22 in November 2025. [[5, 6]]
- **Traffic CTR:** typically **1%–2%**; 1.71% is the current broad US benchmark. [[1]]
- **Lead-ad CTR:** roughly **2%–3%**, with visual categories sometimes above 3.5%. [[1]]
- **CPC:** about **$0.70** for traffic campaigns and **$1.92** for lead campaigns; industry lead CPC ranges from $0.74 in restaurants to $9.78 in dental. [[2]]
- **Conversion rate:** approximately **1.5%–1.6% for e-commerce purchases** versus **7.72% for lead campaigns**. [[4]]
- **CPA:** approximately **$39 for e-commerce purchases**; **$27.66 is the average lead cost**, but lead CPL ranges from about **$3 to $77** by industry. [[3, 2]]

**Interpretation:** Do not compare a $0.70 traffic CPC with a $1.92 lead CPC or a $39 purchase CPA as if they measure the same outcome. For budgeting, use the benchmark matching your optimization event—**link click, lead, qualified lead, purchase, or subscription**—and compare against your own allowable CPA or customer lifetime value.

# Facebook Ads Benchmarks 2025: Data, Trends, & Insights for Your Industry
## About the Author
#### Connect with the author
We’ve got the answers to all these questions and more in this year’s annual Facebook ads benchmarks report, analyzing data from over 1,000 campaigns to provide you with industry-specific KPIs including average cost per click (CPC), click-through rate (CTR), conversion rate (CVR), and cost per lead (CPL) for two core Facebook ads campaign objectives: traffic and leads.
## Key trends: The big picture
- **Facebook Lead Ads click-through rates increased for 9 out of 15 industries**, with an overall slight increase year over year. This shows that Facebook users are still engaging with ads on the Meta platform.
- **The cost per click for Facebook leads objective campaigns increased overall**, but 10 out of 15 industries (67%) saw stable or decreased CPCs.
Advertising costs are increasing across the board—87% of industries saw increases in CPC for Google Ads, with an overall increase of 12.88%. Lead Ads saw a slower rate of increase—only 2.13% compared to 2024. And CPC is still relatively low for Lead Ads at $1.92, compared to $5.26 in Google Ads.
## Facebook ads benchmarks: Traffic campaigns
### Average click-through rate for traffic campaigns
Click-through rate is a core metric when it comes to traffic campaigns because, after all, they’re optimized for clicks.

**The average click-through rate in Facebook ads for traffic campaigns across all industries is 1.71%.** This is higher than last year’s overall average of 1.57%.

## Are Facebook Ads Getting More Expensive?
**Traffic campaigns got cheaper.** CPC dropped from $0.77 to $0.70 (-9%) and CTR improved from 1.57% to 1.71% year-over-year (as of mid-2025, per WordStream). Fewer advertisers are running traffic-only campaigns because they don't drive conversions, which reduced auction pressure.
**Lead campaigns got more expensive.** CPL jumped 21% to $27.66 and CPC rose slightly to $1.92 (as of mid-2025, per WordStream). More advertisers are competing for qualified leads, and Meta's lead form improvements made the format more popular — increased demand, higher prices.
## FAQ
### What is a good CTR for Facebook ads?
Above 1.5% is solid for most industries as of early 2026. The platform-wide median is 2.19% for ecommerce (Triple Whale, full-year 2025) and 1.71% for traffic campaigns across all verticals (WordStream, mid-2025). Health & Wellness leads ecommerce at 2.70%.
### What is a good CPC for Facebook ads?
As of mid-2025 (per WordStream), the all-industry average for traffic campaigns is $0.70 and for lead campaigns it's $1.92. "Good" depends on what that click is worth to you.
### What is a good conversion rate for Facebook ads?
As of early 2026, the ecommerce purchase campaign median is 1.60% (Triple Whale, full-year 2025). For lead generation, the all-industry average is 7.72% (WordStream, mid-2025). Top performers like Restaurants & Food hit 18.25% on lead forms.

# Facebook Ads Cost in 2026: CPC, CPM & CPA by Industry
## What do Facebook ads cost in 2026?
The table below aggregates LocaliQ's Facebook advertising benchmarks (updated October 2025, the most recent full-cycle dataset available, also published by WordStream), which measure the average Facebook ads CPC for traffic and lead campaigns and the average cost per lead across US advertisers.
## What is a good Facebook CPM in 2026?
There is no single Facebook CPM, but the sourced ranges bracket it well. Gupta Media's tracker, built on tens of billions of Meta ad impressions, put the average Meta CPM at $8.19 in October 2025, with an average cost per link click of $0.37.
In ecommerce the picture is more expensive: Triple Whale measured a $14.19 CPM across nearly 35,000 brands in 2025, up 20.03% year over year, with Health & Wellness the steepest riser at $20.70.
## How much does a Facebook lead or purchase cost?
On the purchase side, Triple Whale's 2025 ecommerce dataset shows an average cost per acquisition of $38.19. Looking at Facebook ads CPA by industry within that data, Lifestyle & Boutique ($29.99), Baby ($30.04) and Books & Music ($30.25) buy customers cheapest, while Electronics pays the most at $49.48.
## Frequently asked questions
### What is the average cost per click on Facebook?
LocaliQ's 2025 benchmark data puts the average Facebook CPC at $0.70 for traffic campaigns and $1.92 for lead campaigns. The cheapest industry (Shopping, Collectibles and Gifts) averages $0.34 per traffic click, while Dentists and Dental Services pay $9.78 per click on lead campaigns.
### Are Facebook ads cheaper than Google Ads?
For lead generation, usually yes. LocaliQ's 2025 data puts Facebook's average cost per lead at $27.66 against $70.11 for Google Ads, roughly 61% cheaper.
## Sources and methodology
- LocaliQ, Facebook Advertising Benchmarks (updated October 2025): CPC, cost per lead, and industry breakdowns across US advertisers.
- WordStream, Facebook Ads Benchmarks 2025: the same dataset with year-over-year trend detail.
- Triple Whale, Facebook Ad Benchmarks by Industry (Jan-Dec 2025, ~35,000 ecommerce brands): CPM, CPA, and industry inflation figures.
